title: A brake for pathogen-induced reactive oxygen species burst
content: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are central for plant immunity and, as such, need to be kept in check until they are needed. In Arabidopsis, the braking mechanism is well described: under resting conditions, PBS1-like kinase 13 (PBL13) phosphorylates the C-terminus of the NADPH oxidase RBOHD, the E3 ligase PIRE ubiquitinates it, and the protein is turned over (Lee et al 2020). Upon pathogen perception, ROS signaling mediates the activation of different kinases such as AtBIK1, AtCPK5, AtDORN1, and AtSIK1 (Li et al 2014; Kadota et al 2014; Kobayashi et al 2012; Chen et al 2017; Zhang et al 2018).
